text: In a recorded lecture, S-rank summoner Park Doyun demonstrated seven perfectly coordinated constructs. They felt neither pain nor fear. Sending them inside spared people the danger.
At two forty-six, an exhausted Taeo was still watching. He hadn't felt Nib once during the tunnel survey, and he couldn't stop thinking about it.
From beneath his blanket, Nib demanded that Taeo turn off the shouting brick. Taeo apologised and asked for one more lecture.
Doyun advised listeners to question their own desires when a construct appeared to want something. Nib supplied his own desire without difficulty: 'I want sleep.'
The next morning, Nib asked about the missing porter. There was no update. The company still maintained that he had left voluntarily.
Once Taeo explained that voluntarily meant by choice, Nib asked who had seen him leave. The report named no witness. Nib wasn't satisfied with the claim.
Nib also confirmed that he had pressed the tunnel wall, just as he had at Taeo's store. Taeo had felt nothing. Nib told him to find out why.
At the yard, the mule kept walking into plywood. Taeo suggested giving it one command at a time. Its summoner said stop, and it stopped.
Haein recognised Doyun's influence immediately. Taeo had watched all twelve lectures. His face showed exactly how much sleep that had cost.
He tried the lecture's focused attention on Nib. Nothing happened. Nib pointed out the problem: 'I'm not in lecture four.'
Taeo described the disappearing pulse to Haein. She asked whether it had faded or stopped instantly. He'd been too frightened to notice. She proposed measuring it.
Minho arrived rejecting a C-grade job at its offered rate. He allowed an hour with the training gate. Radios reported positions, but couldn't warn him when a scout's support slipped.
The little licensed gate suited Nib perfectly. Its boss was a snail. Minho's rule was simple: nobody stepped on it. Killing it would close the gate and cost their licence.
Three identical beams supported sandbags. Nib would secretly remove one pin, then test each beam. Blindfolded outside, Taeo had to identify which one slipped. They would try three runs.
The blindfold was a sock. Haein assured Taeo it was clean, then qualified that reassurance with 'Mostly.'
Nib set his terms before entering. Taeo was not to guess. If he felt nothing, he had to say nothing. Taeo agreed.
Haein started the first run. Nib crossed, and the familiar amber glow faded out of Taeo's palm again.
Inside the stone hollow, beneath a green sky, Nib removed the middle beam's pin. Nearby, the snail continued eating lichen.
Outside, an amber pressure flickered back into Taeo's hand. He concentrated on one beam at a time and reported that the first held.
Nib leaned on the middle beam. Its foot slid, and Taeo felt the pressure drag sideways across his palm. He called beam two.
Nib knocked before coming out and raised two fingers. Haein confirmed the match. Taeo's first call had been correct.
On the second run, Taeo felt nothing. The seconds passed. When Haein asked for a call, he offered a hesitant two.
Nib emerged holding up one finger. Taeo had guessed. Haein told him not to apologise to the data, and Nib asked to try again.
For the third run, Taeo breathed slowly and reminded himself not to guess. This time, he clearly felt the first two beams hold.
Holding the connection took effort. A thin line of blood started from Taeo's nose before he noticed anything was wrong.
Inside, the third beam kicked out. Nib caught the falling plank on his shoulder and stopped a tumbling sandbag with his foot, just short of the snail.
Pressure slammed across Taeo's palm, then vanished. He shouted for Nib and beam three, sprang from the crate, and crossed the chalk line while still blindfolded.
Minho caught him just short of the rim. He held Taeo firmly across the chest while everyone waited for an answer.
Nib came out unhurt and raised three fingers. Taeo pulled off the sock and grinned. Two correct calls out of three tests.
Haein pointed out his nosebleed. Taeo touched his lip, saw the blood, and lost the grin.
Nib tilted Taeo's head forward and supplied a napkin. Asked whether the link caused the bleeding, Taeo said he didn't know. Nib approved that answer.
Their result was limited but real: Taeo could feel Nib's pressure across the gate for a few seconds at a time. Minho studied the footprints beyond the line.
The snail had survived. Minho assigned his newest white hair to Taeo, whose attempt to reach the gate had earned it.
That afternoon, Bluebird arrived to repossess one of the family's three vans. The towing fee, another two hundred and twenty thousand won, would be added to their debt.
Before the van went, Haein rescued her father's field notebooks. Bluebird would not be taking those.
It had been Dongsik's first van. Nib's hand moved toward his knife, and Taeo rested a hand on his shoulder. Minho said Bluebird could take it. They owed the money.
The truck left an empty space between the remaining vans. Nib stood in that space, watching where it had gone.
By evening, Minho had accepted the Guro job. Haein reminded him he'd refused it that morning. He answered, 'That was this morning.'
Thursday's job was a C-grade gate in a Guro construction pit, with porters from Dokgo Contracting. Taeo recognised the company from the missing worker's story.
Minho already knew which company it was. His tired expression made clear that the decision hadn't come easily.
He offered Nib the scouting work directly. Nib immediately accepted. Then Minho turned to Taeo and told him to stay outside.
Taeo answered defensively that he always stayed outside.
Minho pointed at the sneaker prints crossing the broken chalk line toward the gate. Then he repeated the instruction, with Taeo looking at the evidence: 'You stay outside.'
